lines.text: After Joseph was born, Jacob asked Laban to send him home, but Laban asked him to stay.
Jacob asked for the speckled, spotted and dark-colored animals as his wages for shepherding Laban's flocks.
That day Laban placed the spotted animals under his sons' care and put a seven-day journey between himself and Jacob.
Jacob peeled fresh poplar, almond and plane branches, set them in the watering troughs, and the flocks bore speckled young.
Jacob set out the branches only for the stronger animals, so he became prosperous with flocks, servants, camels and horses.
